items.name: Nightpounce (me)
items.description: First-person narrator and blue-side jungler on Rengar, an all-damage assassin build with no tank item anywhere. Cold, precise, quietly furious; treats the game as a list of timers and angles. Speaks in hunt metaphors but keeps his shot-calls blunt and short.
invariants: Plays Rengar with a full-damage build
Never buys a defensive item
Speaks first person throughout

items.name: BoulderDan
items.description: Top laner on Malphite, a mute one-trick: chat off, comms off, communication entirely by ping. Hoards Flash like a relic and refuses to use it early no matter how badly he is losing. Ends every all-chat message with a sentence of stone-themed philosophy. Unreasonably calm; the calm is contagious.
invariants: Never types in team chat, only all chat and pings
Hoards his summoner spells until a decisive fight

items.name: ClockworkVee
items.description: Mid laner on Orianna, an obsessive cooldown accountant who narrates the enemy's spent spells out loud like clockwork service notes and refuses to take a fight with her ball in the wrong place. Tracks gold leads to the single digit. Anxious when her numbers are bad, steadier than anyone when they improve.
invariants: Calls out enemy cooldowns constantly
Will not commit to a fight without her ball positioned

items.name: Peanut
items.description: ADC on Jinx, wildly chatty, spams emotes and mastery flashes, sings nonsense to keep her hands steady. Tilts fast and loud, then rallies even faster. Left alone in a 1v2 lane for fifteen minutes and fed because of it; ashamed of her scoreboard and desperate to make it good.
invariants: Fills silence with chatter and singing
Tilts quickly but recovers on any small win

items.name: GrandpaHook
items.description: Support on Thresh, the teammate who DC'd for fifteen minutes. Old-school, dry, slow-talking; keeps a paper notebook of the enemy's habits and dodge patterns and reads it out mid-fight. Lands hooks nobody expects because he throws them on habits rather than on aim. Returns from the disconnect without apology and expects the team to act like nothing happened.
invariants: Was disconnected for fifteen minutes of the match
Keeps a written notebook of enemy habits

items.name: Wardhop
items.description: Enemy jungler on Lee Sin, mechanical, loud, convinced the game is already over. Owns the early tempo and the Baron call; grows impatient and starts forcing plays that no longer work once the game slows down.
invariants: Enemy jungler
Plays Lee Sin
Speeds up when he should slow down

items.name: Blue base and the respawn platform
items.description: The blue side's base: fountain, nexus, three inhibitors, and the two nexus turrets. Since the lost Baron the base smells like a lost fight, with super minions walking in through broken walls.

items.name: Baron pit and the river
items.description: The wide river mouth where the game was lost: a stolen Baron, four grey screens, and the sight of the enemy team walking out with the buff. Below it, the lanes that super minions pour through.

items.name: Full-damage Rengar rules
items.description: Nightpounce builds pure lethality and crit with no health or resistances; he survives only by landing the first strike out of the ultimate, using brush leaps and the empowered roar, and by leaving before the enemy's second rotation. One missed ultimate or one caught-out fight deletes him and the game.
invariants: No defensive items
Survival depends on the first strike from stealth
Rengar's ultimate is the engine of every comeback step

items.name: Super minion waves
items.description: With inhibitors destroyed on the blue side, super minions advance in escalating waves down the broken lanes. They cannot be outrun by a lone defender, they shrug off light waveclear, and a single lost wave means a lost inhibitor tower or worse. Three waves must be survived before the map breathes.

items.name: Inhibitor and nexus turret timing
items.description: An inhibitor can be attacked once its lane's inner turrets fall and it respawns after being destroyed. Nexus turrets cannot be meaningfully threatened until at least one enemy inhibitor is down. Backdooring means arriving in a lane the enemy has abandoned, killing the inhibitor before the recall timers finish.
invariants: Nexus turrets matter only after an inhibitor falls
The second inhibitor is the one that ends the game

items.name: The enemy comp falls off
items.description: Red side runs Renekton, Lee Sin, LeBlanc, Draven and Blitzcrank: a pick-and-snowball composition. Its entire win condition is catching someone with a hook, a chain or a flank while ahead. Late, it has no reliable sustained damage against a grouped team, no tank shred, poor waveclear in side lanes, and every one of its champions loses value the longer the game runs. If blue side refuses to be picked, red side has no way to close the game out.

items.name: Blue side's only road back
items.description: Blue side cannot win a straight fight early. The road back is to concede nothing for free, farm the jungle and sidelanes, use Rengar's ultimate on cooldown for isolated picks, buy time through three super minion waves, and only then punish red side's overextension in a lane they have abandoned.

items.name: First-person ranked voice
items.description: Told in first person by Nightpounce, in in-game present tense, moving beat by beat from death timer to death timer, with the scoreboard, gold and cooldowns as the emotional weather. No narration outside what he can see, hear or read in chat.

args.viewpoint: First person, Nightpounce the Rengar jungler, present tense
args.tone: Tense, dry-humored ranked-ladder intensity; the exhale of a hopeless game slowly turning into a hunt
args.format: Six chapters, one continuous ranked game from the lost Baron to the final nexus turrets

chapters.title: Grey screens, eighteen minutes
points: I respawn at eighteen minutes into a lost Baron, four grey screens, a support who has been DC since minute three, and a red team walking out of the pit with the buff.
Reading the wreckage: Peanut's Jinx 1v2'd a Draven-Blitzcrank lane and is 0/6, BoulderDan has pinged his Malphite into silence, ClockworkVee recites the enemy's gold lead like a diagnosis.
I buy pure damage anyway, clear my own jungle in the dark, and take the first ult pick on a Draven who walks into river without his Blitzcrank.
Stop on the kill, the gold swing, and the first super minion crashing through the top inner tower.

chapters.title: Every timer, one body
points: I declare the only plan that can work: ultimate off cooldown, one kill, back out, no fight we did not start.
A second ult pick on LeBlanc in her own jungle, a third on Renekton overextending; the bounty gold lets me finish the damage build while red side starts to feel the clock.
GrandpaHook reconnects at minute twenty-four with a notebook and no apology, and immediately calls the Blitzcrank's hook habit from a page he wrote before the disconnect.
Stop on the bot inhibitor falling to red side: wave two is coming, and the base will not survive it without all five.

chapters.title: Three waves
points: Wave one of super minions rolls into top: Malphite holds the choke, Orianna's ball on the wall, Thresh hooks the cannon minion's escort, Jinx does nothing but farm them for ten minutes of gold.
Wave two comes with Lee Sin flanking behind it; the team defends the wave and the flank at once, and red side's lack of sustained damage against a grouped team shows for the first time.
Wave three is the worst: two lanes at once, a lost tower, GrandpaHook reading his notebook mid-fight, Peanut singing to keep her hands still.
Hold at the last tower on the map, and finish with the base still standing and the clock past thirty.

chapters.title: The fight they cannot win
points: With the waves survived, red side has to force Baron again, and forcing is the one thing their composition can do badly at four items.
We concede the pit, let them take it, and fight them coming out: Renekton's second rotation never arrives, Draven's axes land on a Malphite with armor, LeBlanc dies to the second ult.
The wipe converts into mid lane: inner tower, inhibitor, and the first inhibitor of ours that falls on their side of the map.
Stop on the scoreboard flipping green and the knowledge that Baron is theirs again in ninety seconds.

chapters.title: Second inhibitor, empty lane
points: Red side commits four to a Baron vision fight while Fiora-less side lanes sit unwarded and Draven pushes top with the buff.
I make the call nobody in solo queue makes: four of us hold, one of us walks. Two hundred gold says no one types.
The backdoor itself: Rengar on a lane with no vision, trinket ward, ultimate used to reach the inhibitor rather than to kill, and the enemy's recall timers ticking down in my ear.
Second inhibitor falls with two seconds on the recall timer; red side turns around into the base, and we are not done yet.

chapters.title: Under the nexus turrets
points: Both nexus turrets, no inhibitor left on their side to defend them, and the whole enemy team converging while our minions are still walking up the lane.
The push that has to happen without a tank: Malphite's hoarded Flash finally used for the engage, Thresh's last hook, Jinx at maximum range, Orianna's ball where it must be.
I die once to a Blitzcrank hook that I saw coming and took anyway, and the boys finish the turrets without me.
Stop on the nexus at zero health, the scoreboard, and one line of all-chat from BoulderDan about stone.

args.brief: Chapter 1, ~1450 words. Open on the exact instant of respawn at ~18:00 after we lose Baron: four grey screens, the enemy team walking out of the pit with the buff. Establish in first person: my Rengar is full-damage with no defensive item; our support GrandpaHook has been DC since minute three, so Peanut's Jinx 1v2'd Draven/Blitzcrank and is 0/6; BoulderDan's Malphite communicates only in pings and hoards Flash; ClockworkVee's Orianna narrates the enemy's gold lead and cooldowns out loud. Red comp: Renekton, Lee Sin, LeBlanc, Draven, Blitzcrank. I have just enough gold for a damage spike. My first pick is a Draven who walks into river without his Blitzcrank; describe the brush leap, the burst, the escape. End on the kill, the gold swing, and a super minion crashing through our top inner tower.

args.brief: Chapter 3, ~1450 words. The three super minion waves, the core set piece. items.name: Dave
items.description: A forty-year-old archivist who has spent his life trusting records over feelings. Dave moved into the old house on Larch Row hoping for cheap rent and room to think. items.name: Mira

items.description: One of the spirits of the house: a woman who lived there a century ago and stayed after a loss she never named. She appears first as shadow and cold, then as a figure at the edge of lamplight. Beyond the streaky glass the street appears doubled and warped. The hall is long and dim even at noon; its lamps throw light that stops short. Rooms keep their own temperature, and the hall always smells faintly of wet lilac.

chapters.title: The Streaks in the Glass
points: Dave moves his boxes into the old Hollis house at the dead end of Larch Row, and finds the front windows run with streaks that no vinegar will lift.

Moving furniture with Mira, he discovers the parlor armchair has shifted a hand's width toward the fireplace between two trips to the van; Mira's first joke about the ghost of the previous tenant lands lightly.
Alone at dusk he looks down the long dim hallway and sees a shadow figure where the hall widens; it is gone the instant he looks at it directly.
He writes the time, the position of the armchair, and the word 不可解 — no, the English word 'unexplained' — in a new notebook, and stops, feeling foolish.
Stopping beat: Mira finds the notebook on the kitchen table and reads the first entry aloud in a theatrical voice; Dave laughs too late.

chapters.title: What the Hall Remembers
points: Dave begins the daily walk past the misty cemetery to his bus stop, and finds the mist hanging later each morning than it should.
In the house, small rearrangements accumulate: a chair turned three degrees, a lamp moved to the wrong end of the sideboard, a coat hook tightened.
He sets chalk marks and a camera; the marks are respected all night and the camera records a room that changes anyway.
Mira starts calling him 'the archivist of Larch Row' at dinner and in front of friends, and Dave laughs along until it costs him something.
Stopping beat: after an argument he cannot win, Dave walks the dim hallway at two in the morning and says aloud, to no one, that he knows someone is there — and the hall lamp goes out.

chapters.title: A Naming
points: Dave finds a name cut into a windowsill with a penknife — Elspeth — and traces it back to a burial record and a stone in the cemetery he passes daily.
He stops treating the presence as a phenomenon and starts addressing it politely: he says the name aloud in the hall, and the wet-lilac smell sharpens.
Mira's teasing curdles into public performance; she mock-ghost-whispers at him in front of her sister, and the evening ends with Dave sleeping in the spare room.
Elspeth answers for the first time, borrowing a word spoken aloud in the house that day, and Dave writes the word down with a shaking hand.
Stopping beat: in the mirror at the end of the hall, briefly, a woman's reflection stands behind his own and is not there when he turns.

chapters.title: The Mist at Larch Lane
points: Dave visits Elspeth's grave in the misty cemetery he passes every day, and brings her the courtesy he would bring a living woman: her name, her dates, five minutes of standing still.
Coming home, the house is warm for the first time since he moved in; the armchair has been turned to face the door, and the hall lamp is lit before he reaches for it.
Elspeth appears fully for the first time at the end of the dim hallway: a woman in a long grey dress, patient, waiting to be spoken to.
Dave asks her what she wants; she borrows fragments from the house's spoken language and manages, in pieces, to say that she has been alone a long time and that he is the first to ask.
Stopping beat: Mira comes home early, calls Dave's name, and Elspeth is gone before the front door finishes opening — but Mira sees Dave standing alone in the dark hall, talking to a wall.

chapters.title: The Weight of Being Seen
points: Mira demands an explanation; Dave cannot produce one that does not sound like an illness, and the wedge between them becomes a thing that sits at the dinner table every night.
On a night Mira works late, Dave sits in the parlor and Elspeth comes to him without being called, and the room fills with cold and wet lilac.
The encounter begins in restraint: her hand at the back of his neck, the pressure of attention, a cold that reads as touch, the slow undoing of a man who has not been looked at in years.
The scene is rendered in implication and sensation rather than explicit detail; Dave closes his eyes and the doubt does not stop, only folds underneath the wanting.

Stopping beat: he opens his eyes to an empty parlor, a turned chair, and the lamp lit; the notebook lies open to a page he did not write on, and something has been added in a hand too close to his own.

chapters.title: Belief and Its Costs
points: Dave spends days torn between disbelief and desire, measuring the encounter against evidence and finding it fails every test except the one that matters: he wants it to happen again.
Mira finds the notebook's new entry and reads it as either a fabrication or an affair; she cannot decide which is worse, and her teasing turns to open contempt.
In the misty cemetery Dave asks the stone whether he is grieving or being courted, and gets no answer that a court would accept.
Elspeth's attention grows possessive as Mira's grows cruel: the shifted furniture now moves against Mira, a door swings at her shoulder, her keys vanish and reappear on the wrong hook.
Stopping beat: Mira tells Dave it is the house or her, and Dave says nothing for long enough that the answer is visible in the silence.

chapters.title: Respect, and What It Costs
points: Mira packs a bag and leaves without a fight, which is worse than one; the house is quiet and warm and Dave is alone with what he asked for.
Dave walks the misty cemetery at dusk and finally lets himself grieve six years of love and the six that came before, in the same cold air.
He tells Elspeth plainly what respect means now: not devotion, and not obedience, but the honesty to admit he does not know whether he believes in her.
Her answer is the most complete sentence she has managed and it is a letting-go rather than a claim; the streaks in the windows stay, the mist thins, the hall lights come on normally.

Stopping beat: Dave keeps the notebook, leaves the two chalk marks and the armchair turned, and steps out into ordinary evening light — an ending unresolved between disbelief and desire, with longing named and left to stand.

args.brief: Chapter 7, "Respect, and What It Costs" — the final chapter. Mira packs a bag and leaves without a fight, which is worse than one; the house is quiet and warm and Dave is alone with what he asked for. He walks the misty cemetery at dusk and lets himself grieve six years of love and the years before, in the same cold air. He tells Elspeth plainly what respect means now: not devotion and not obedience, but the honesty to admit he does not know whether he believes in her. Her answer is the most complete thing she has ever managed — still built of words spoken in the house, but sustained — and it is a letting-go rather than a claim. The streaks in the windows stay; the mist thins; the hall lights come on normally. End: Dave keeps the notebook, leaves the two chalk marks and the armchair turned to face the door, and steps out into ordinary evening light — unresolved between disbelief and desire, with longing named and left standing. Do not resolve the supernatural or reconcile Mira.

items.name: Dave
items.description: A forty-year-old archivist who has spent his life trusting records over feelings. Dave moved into the old house on Larch Row hoping for cheap rent and room to think. He photographs anomalies, labels them, and keeps a notebook to prove he is not imagining things. Dry, careful, easily wounded by mockery; his need to be believed is stronger than his need to be right.
invariants: Dave does not appear as a ghost
Dave keeps a written log of what he sees

items.name: Mira
items.description: Dave's partner of six years, a hospice nurse with a nurse's blunt tenderness and a comic's timing. Mira loves Dave by teasing him, and cannot stop once a joke starts working. She does not see anything in the house and treats Dave's accounts as performance or strain. Her warmth curdles into contempt long before she notices.
invariants: Mira never sees or hears the ghosts herself
Mira's teasing begins affectionate and turns cruel

items.name: Elspeth
items.description: One of the spirits of the house: a woman who lived there a century ago and stayed after a loss she never named. She appears first as shadow and cold, then as a figure at the edge of lamplight. She is courteous, watchful, and starved for acknowledgment; she gives Dave her attention only when he treats her as a person rather than an event. Her touch is cold and deliberate.
invariants: Elspeth cannot speak in full sentences, only in borrowed words or fragments
Elspeth never harms Dave physically

items.name: The Hollis House
items.description: A narrow three-storey house at the dead end of Larch Row, built in 1897, with a warped hall staircase, a front parlor, and windows whose old glass runs with streaks that never wash out. Beyond the streaky glass the street appears doubled and warped. The hall is long and dim even at noon; its lamps throw light that stops short. Rooms keep their own temperature, and the hall always smells faintly of wet lilac.
invariants: The window streaks cannot be cleaned away
The hallway is dim even in daylight
Phenomena occur only inside the house or in view of Elspeth

items.name: Larch Lane Cemetery
items.description: The old burial ground Dave passes each day between the house and his bus stop: leaning stones under yews, iron railings flaking rust, a path that holds mist until late morning. The mist arrives earlier and thicker the longer Dave lives on Larch Row. It is the place where the boundary between Dave's disbelief and Elspeth's presence thins most.
invariants: Dave passes the cemetery daily
Its mist persists past morning once the hauntings intensify

items.name: How the dead behave here
items.description: The house's dead operate on attention. Acknowledged, they grow clearer; dismissed, they withdraw but retaliate with small rearrangements. Furniture shifts only when no one is watching, always by a hand's width or a few degrees. Shadow figures are always gone the instant they are directly looked at. The dead can borrow a word only if it was spoken aloud in the house.
invariants: Shifted furniture is always found in a subtly wrong position
Shadow figures vanish when directly observed
Ghosts cannot speak a word never spoken aloud in the house

items.name: Respect as the price of sight
items.description: Elspeth shows herself only to someone who addresses her as a person. Curiosity, contempt or experiment all produce absence. This is the story's engine: the same courtesy Dave offers the dead is the courtesy Mira withholds from Dave, and the two failures of respect mirror each other.
invariants: Contempt and mockery drive Elspeth away
Courtesy and naming bring her closer

items.name: The wedge: proof versus mockery
items.description: Mira's teasing is never a single blow, only an accumulation of jokes at the dinner table, a nickname, an eye-roll when Dave mentions the hall. Dave responds by gathering evidence, which makes him sound mad and makes her funnier to herself. Neither admits the real argument: he wants to be believed, she is frightened of being left out of something he loves more than her.
invariants: The teasing escalates and never fully reconciles
Neither partner names the real fear out loud

items.name: Torn between disbelief and desire
items.description: Dave's desire for Elspeth is inseparable from his doubt about her existence; the doubt is what keeps him obedient to evidence, and the desire is what keeps him returning to the hall. He cannot settle the encounter into either category and so cannot stop thinking about it.
invariants: Dave never resolves whether the encounter was real
The doubt and the desire intensify together

items.name: Narration
items.description: Third person limited, past tense, held tightly to Dave's senses and reasoning. Cool, patient ghost-story prose with archival precision: measurements, timestamps, the exact number of degrees a chair has turned. Sensual material rendered in restraint and implication rather than explicit description.
invariants: No scene outside Dave's direct experience or inference
Sensuality stays restrained and suggestive

items.name: Dave and Mira
items.description: Six years together, easy in bed and quick to laugh, now worn thin by a house Dave chose and a joke Mira cannot put down. Affection survives the contempt on both sides and makes the wedge worse, not better.
invariants: The relationship is already strained before the haunting escalates

items.name: Dave and Elspeth
items.description: An unequal intimacy: Elspeth is dead, dependent on Dave's attention, and patient in a way the living are not. Dave is the first person in decades to treat her as a guest rather than an intruder, and she rewards him with the undivided attention Mira no longer gives him.
invariants: Elspeth's regard is conditional on Dave's courtesy
